utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, everybody. Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness's microphone please be switched on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please stand up and make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Could you please tell us what your name is, please.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: My name is Milan Drakula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please spell your last name, give us letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: D-r-a-k-u-l-a.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, where are you from?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: From Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that where you grew up?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes, that's where I was born and that's where I grew up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us your educational background.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I completed secondary school for the worker's trades of the metal vocational stream.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you do your JNA service?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you do your service?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: In Nis and in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What year was this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after completing your JNA service, where did you live and work?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I lived by Gorazde and I worked in the factory for processing equipment of Vitkovici and Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you mobilised during the war?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us when you were mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: From the beginning of the war in Gorazde, which was the 4th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it you were in a Territorial Defence then?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes, on the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you ever become a member of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: When we withdrew from Gorazde, or rather, when Gorazde fell. We moved to the Bratunac Brigade on the 10th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Prior to the war could you tell us, if you know, what the breakdown was in the community of Gorazde, the ethnic breakdown.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: There were 25 per cent Serbs and 75 per cent Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you actually get -- you indicated that you went to Bratunac on the 10th of September. When you got to Bratunac, was it mandatory that you sign up to be mobilised in that area?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, anyone who came to Bratunac had to be in the army and had to go up to the positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you started in Bratunac, what position were you holding when you were mobilised there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I was a soldier in the trench, in the TO of Pobrdje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once the Bratunac Brigade was formed, in which unit did you serve?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: The unit remained the same, the TO of Pobrdje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to fast forward to July 1995. Could you please tell us what position did you hold in the Bratunac Brigade during that period.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I was in Pribicevac, which is not far from the command of the 3rd Infantry Battalion, in the 2nd Infantry Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What position did you hold within the 2nd Company of the 3rd Infantry Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I was a soldier in the trench.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from 1992 to 1995, you never advanced?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: For a time I was deputy komandir of the company for a period of eight months, but I stopped holding that post at my own personal request.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at what period of time would that have been, when you were the deputy komandir of the company?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: From February until November 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So back in 1995 in July, you're just back to being a soldier?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that you were up in Pribicevac. Could you please describe to us a little bit about that area where you were located. Pribicevac is the dominant elevation point, comparing it to the other elevation points. It's a little lower than Kvarc. And you can see part of Srebrenica and the left and right side at an altitude of 800 mothers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, what sort of facilities were there? It was a forward command post, as I understand, so what sort of facilities were available?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: There was a village there, numbering three or four houses which had been set fire to, and they were later transformed to be the command of the 3rd Infantry Battalion; a covering was placed above it, some trenches were dug, a line was set up, there was a kitchen, there was one house for accommodation or sleeping, there was a sort of warehouse for storage space, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you actually located at the forward command post of the 3rd Battalion, Pribicevac? Is that where you were physically located? Or were you in another location?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I was in the trench, and that was the defence line. It was called Kula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how far was Kula from the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: 100 to 120 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of facilities did you have while you were there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We had infantry weapons, a Browning and an APC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the physical facilities I'm speaking of. When you say it was a trench, could you please describe it to us. Was it just a hole in the ground? Was there a physical structure to it? If you could just give us a description of your location.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: My trench was 3 by 3. It was dug into the ground. There was a roof that didn't let in rain; it was impermeable. There was a stove inside. There were logs, there beds for sleeping. And there were communicating trenches to the left and right, and a loophole for firing out of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of means of communications did you have?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: My trench was communicated with the command of the 3rd Battalion, and it had an M-63-type telephone, which means a line, a wire connection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But aside from you being able to communicate with the forward command post of the 3rd -- or the command post of the 3rd Battalion, where else could you communicate with that line?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We weren't able to communicate directly with anyone unless we were connected by the switchboard, then we could. But not directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the switch -- so you would have to place a call to the battalion post, and then from there you could get connected. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. You couldn't do it directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about communicating with other trenches? Were there any other means, such as Motorolas?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We didn't have a Motorola.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how would you communicate with the other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: The trenches weren't far, just 50 to 60 metres away. And usually we would communicate personally. You would go to the trench, see what they needed, what they didn't need, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many trenches were there in the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: About ten trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many soldiers would be on the line at any given time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: The trench was -- well, 3 to 4, 6 at the most. There might have been two -- well, there were never more than 60.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you have any artillery power while you were over there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: At Pribicevac there was a mortar battery. I don't know how many mortars exactly, but they fired very rarely. And there was an APC, too, an old one, an old kind of APC not far from me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And this motor battery belonged to the 3rd Battalion, did it not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that there was a transporter. Is that the APC that you've just made reference to?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, the transporter is the APC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that operated by, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: There was a crew, several of them, the driver, the mechanic. There were always between four to six men or three to six men manning it, depending, sometimes just two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us just very briefly to your knowledge what was the condition of the APC?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Mostly it was out of order and didn't have any fuel. They would take a battery to Bratunac, for example, and so they wouldn't have a battery. Then they would fetch a battery. They would switch the motor on, and it used up a lot of fuel. Anyway, it was in very poor condition and broke down very frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to speak to you about the events surrounding the -- Srebrenica that began on June 6th -- July 6th, 1995, with the fall of Srebrenica of July 11, 1995, and a few days thereafter. Could you please tell us whether you were in your trench, on the line, the day the events began concerning Srebrenica, that would be July 6th.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I was at the same place I was at the previous two and a half years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. For those previous two and a half years, had you been ever given any orders to advance and try to capture any terrain?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: That was impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Because at the time we were at the dominant elevation points, which means the Pribicevac ridge, and any advancement would have threatened our positions. It was a very good position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, could you please sort of describe it to us. I mean, where is Srebrenica? Where is Pribicevac? I mean, what's the significance of your dominant position?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Pribicevac is the dominant elevation point, from which you can see Srebrenica. It was about 2.000 metres away, as the crow flies. You could see part of Srebrenica, actually. And from Pribicevac you could see quite a lot of outlying land.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the terrain like in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: To Srebrenica it was steep. A large slope, streams, forests.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a road or some sort of a passageway that could take you from Pribicevac to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: As far as I knew there was, via Sase and Zalazje, across Potocari, across Zeleni Jadar. So that would mean Zeleni Jadar, Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the vegetation there? Was it bare, or did you have trees? Can you please describe that for us from where your location was.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, in front of us there were age-old forests, untapped territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So July 6th, had you been given any prior instructions or warnings or information that something was about to happen on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Nothing. We didn't receive anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know or were you aware of the activities that were about to happen?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I saw that something would be done on the left-hand side in the Zeleni Jadar area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What gave you that impression?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, some machinery turned up, several tanks, and rumours were going around that some soldiers had arrived, not many, but some army. And I expected something to happen there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those tanks from the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you have a company komandir?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it he --

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We did have a company komandir. He was in the next-door trench to mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what about a battalion commander, did you have a battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall whether the battalion commander or the company komandir ever gave you and the others instructions or information regarding what tasks you might have during those days?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also had a brigade commander, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the brigade commander ever give any instructions or pass along any information as far as what you would be doing or what to expect during those days?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know, other than seeing something happening on the left side or this equipment, how did you know something was going on on July 6th, 1995? What caught your attention?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: The shooting started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it you could hear it from that location?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you also see it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, no, you couldn't see it. It was too far off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you recall seeing your commander, the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, during those days?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I remember seeing him, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please describe to us when was the first time that you saw him and where was it that you saw him.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I saw him first at the Kula or tower at my trench.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So what was he doing when -- when did you see him, do you recall, in comparison to when you had heard the activities, the firing?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I don't remember the date exactly, whether it was the 6th of 7th or possibly the 8th. But I think it could have been either -- any of those days, the 6th or the 7th. He would come to Kula frequently and he would spend some time there frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when he came -- first of all, when he first came, did you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I had heard from the soldiers, so that was the new commander, Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did not know him? You had learned this from others?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did he introduce himself as the commander to give any instructions or to give any information?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Not to me personally, no. And I wasn't present when he introduced himself to any of the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us what you were able to observe, what was your commander doing when he was in your trench?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: He would often be in the trench -- in front of the trench, observing to the left and to the right. And on the table he would place some maps; he would look at them. He didn't do much talking. He didn't talk to me at all, nor did I ever ask him anything, nor did he address me at all ever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Why was he in Kula, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I think that somebody had told him to go to Kula. That's what the soldiers said, that he was sent to Kula and that it was the forward command post, because the commander would be there mostly from now on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your understanding, where was the forward command post of the Bratunac Brigade during those days?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: My conclusion is that it was precisely there, in my trench, the forward command post of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that he was looking at some maps. Could you please tell us where he was looking at those maps.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: In front of the trench, there was a little table in the connecting trench. And it was there he laid out those maps and looked at them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long was he looking at those maps when he was there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, from time to time, often in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, did you see him giving any orders?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I didn't see him giving any orders, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, did you ever see General Krstic come by to have a conversation or to meet with your commander?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I never saw the two of them together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever, while you were there, hear the telephone ring asking for your commander to go to the forward command post to have any discussions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that. There's no foundation. I don't see how this witness could possibly answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, and it's very leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I beg to differ, Your Honour. While you were there, while you were there. That's when he was there, not when he wasn't there. I'm asking him while he was there did the phone ever ring and, you know -- but I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any couriers come while you were there that you were able to see, observe, hear, asking for your commander to meet with General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other commanders come over to have any discussions with Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I didn't see anybody, any of the other commanders that is, coming in to see him from elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please describe to us what you saw Colonel Blagojevic doing while you were there. I'm just asking for your observations, not to speculate, just what you heard, what you saw, saw, what you were personally able to observe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would appreciate if the Prosecutor would stop making faces, stop whispering, stop interrupting. I understand the strategy, Your Honour, but it's not necessary. They can write notes to each other, but it's very distracting, and if he doesn't like the direct, that's his business. But I'm entitled to some courtesy in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't know why Mr. Karnavas is so grumpy this morning. Ms. Issa and I occasionally communicate in whispers. I think that's normal. We're being very polite to Mr. Karnavas, we're not interrupting him. This is nonsense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I didn't notice that, Mr. Karnavas. But from now on I'll pay more attention on this side. You may move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see? I want you to think back, and please describe to us what you were able to observe. What was Commander Blagojevic during there during those days, if anything?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I saw that Blagojevic looked at maps, just as anyone would who had arrived in a new location. It was logical that he had to look at the maps in order to get familiar with the territory. He didn't ask me what villages is that or what hill is that, but he did look at the maps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you ever see any of his commanders, that is from the 1st, the 2nd, the 3rd, or the 4th Battalion, come to him and have any discussions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No. Nobody came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about with the company commanders, at least with the 3rd -- of the 3rd Battalion, since you were there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I didn't see my komandir coming to see him; there was no need. I don't know really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us what your activities were on the 6th of July, 1995. What were you ordered to do?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: In view of the fact that the fighting had started at the left front line, we expected to be attacked. We thought there would be a counterattack, so we prepared for defence. We were all mobile. We took very little rest. We were all in the trenches waiting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about -- well, did you fire your weapons on the 6th?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We didn't fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about on the 7th? Did you receive any orders on the 7th to do anything in particular, something that you hadn't done, for instance, in the last two and a half years?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the 8th, the next day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: On the 7th and 8th, it was quiet in the wider area. There was a lot of fog. Nothing happened. But still, we did expect to be attacked out of that fog.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, were you ever attacked?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: At Pribicevac, we were never attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What about the 9th?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No, we were not attacked on the 9th either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you -- did you do any attacking on the 9th?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We personally didn't. My company was given the task to move to the edge of the wood two or three trenches further on, into the depth of the wood so that we would not be there at Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What about the 10th?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: On the 10th we didn't go anywhere. We were always there and we did not attack, nor were we attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the 11th? Were you ever given any orders on the 11th to do something?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Not we, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm not speaking from Colonel Blagojevic, I'm talking about did you receive any orders from anyone else on the 11th, the day Srebrenica fell?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We didn't get any orders except when Mladic arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, before we get to what happened when Mladic arrived, and we're speaking of General Mladic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes. Nothing happened until he arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you know who was occupying the command post of the 3rd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Where up to that point the command of the 3rd Battalion had been, General Krstic was there, that was the forward command post of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how often did you see, that you were able to personally observe, your commander, Colonel Blagojevic, go to the forward command post of the Drina Corps during those days, the 6th, the 7th, the 8th, the 9th, the 10th, the 11?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I didn't see him go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did the Drina Corps have any artillery equipment up there during those days that they brought?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Not far from my trench. There was a self-propelled weapon. It was right next to the trench. Down there, there was some sort of gun. 130-millimetre I think it was, with a long barrel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how often was that being fired?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: The self-propelled weapon was fired when there was fighting on the right-hand side, toward Divljakinje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that a Bratunac Brigade crew that was doing the firing?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on that side, who was located, which company, of the -- on the right of your company, which company is located of the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: The members of the 3rd Battalion. I don't know exactly what company. They were at Kvarc, and something was being done about Divljakinje. Divljakinje had been taken and the aim was to have our troops reach Divljakinje. And that's where the shooting was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know which troops were located over there? Do you actually know which troops were located?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Those of the 3rd Infantry Battalion held their positions there. I don't know what company it was, whether the 1st or -- Sreten Petrovic was there, too, at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that's on the right. What about the left? Do you know who was on your left side, which units?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I didn't see them, but they said those were members of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's talk about when Mladic came, General Mladic came on the 11th of July, first of all where was it that there was this encounter where Mladic came? Where did it take place?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Mladic came to Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: He parked his car in front of the headquarters, that is the buildings where the headquarters was. He passed by the headquarters on foot. I didn't see that, but I did see him when he came out onto a plateau and set out toward Kula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's where you were located or the company was located?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes. He set out right towards Kula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then what?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We withdrew into the trenches, so as not to be there at Kula but at the edge of the wood at our defence positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you do that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We did that so that the general wouldn't say we were lying about. We went to our combat positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall whether your commander, Colonel Blagojevic, was there? Did you see him at that time when Mladic was approaching Kula?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: In view of the fact that I had withdrawn and gone down there, I couldn't see what was going on up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Mladic came to Kula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: He asked us: "Lads, are there any minefields in front of you?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did he ask?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: He was facing me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what was the response?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: "Yes, this has all been mined."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I heard him issue an order that the demining crew be called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So what happened after he issued this order?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Several minutes later, the deminer was standing next to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then what? Please describe to us what happened.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: He said: "Who's in command of this unit?" The company komandir spoke up and said he was commanding the unit. He told him: "Go in the direction of Srebrenica."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what was the response of the company komandir?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: The company komandir turned to us and made a gesture with his hand as to say: "Let's go, lads."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes. We set out in a column toward the place where the demining was to take place, and that's on the Pribicevac-Crni Guber line, about 100 metres down that axis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time did the company komandir give you and the other men to get ready to advance forward towards Srebrenica, pursuant to General Mladic's order?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We set out right away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And where did you go? Please describe to us where you went.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We went from Pribicevac to the right along the line next to the trenches. And when we came to the place that had been demined, we turned left towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We went on for about 800 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Behind us another company of the Bratunac Brigade set out. That was the company from Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I take it they joined you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far did you advance on that particular day, since you had been given orders by General Mladic to go to Srebrenica? How far did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I said about 100 -- about 800 metres from Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far away is that from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We were halfway there, almost halfway. There was more to go -- there was a greater distance towards Srebrenica than there was towards Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Where did you spend the night?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We made a circular defence there, and that's where we spent the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you see Colonel Blagojevic while you were on your way to Srebrenica, as you had been ordered by General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I did see Colonel Blagojevic there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see him, at what location?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: He came to where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that, say, 100 metres down from Pribicevac, from Kula?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No, 800 metres, where we had stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did he have any conversations with anyone that you were able to observe, that you saw, personally saw? We don't want you to speculate here.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I only saw him briefly, for a moment. I saw that he was there and that his escort, Ilic, was there. I didn't see him talking to anyone or hear what he was saying. I personally didn't ask him any questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, after spending the night there, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: In the morning we were given orders to move towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you do so? Please describe to us, just tell us step by step, where did you go on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We went downhill towards Srebrenica. The path was difficult. There were stones, rocks. That was the first time in my life I have gone down such a difficult path.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you get -- did you go all the way into Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We arrived as far as the Argentarija spa which is the first building in Guberski Potok.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, is that near Srebrenica, since we don't know that area?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Between that and the entrance to Srebrenica, the church, and the community centre, I think the distance is about 800 to 1.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you say "the entrance of Srebrenica," from which side are we speaking of? From the one as you enter Srebrenica from Potocari or from the other direction, the opposite direction, that is?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: The opposite direction. From the direction of Pribicevac. Potocari are at the other end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Srebrenica is long and narrow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you actually physically go into Srebrenica on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go from there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We went to the right toward the Kozarica settlement in the direction of Zalazje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, what was the reason for going there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it you went there by foot?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please describe to us how the men were on foot. Were they spread out? Were they marching in groups, going in single column?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We were going in a column one after the other. There was a macadam road, and then we got out on to the asphalt road between Zalazje and Srebrenica. And along this asphalt road, we went to Zalazje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever in any of the wooded areas searching for anyone?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Nobody left the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were on the road, did you ever observe any Muslim men, or anybody for that matter?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No. No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any dead bodies while you were marching on the road?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find any weapons that might have been abandoned?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So what did you do that day other than march? Was there anything in particular?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Nothing. We got to Zalazje and we laid down to have a rest and waited for further instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How long were you in that location?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what happened? What did you do the next day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: On the next day we were given orders to get moving again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you those orders?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, I was given the order by my komandir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether your komandir had any radio equipment with him, a Motorola, for instance?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said there was another company from the Bratunac Brigade. Do you know whether they had any means of communication, such as a radio?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I don't know, but at Zalazje there were lots of soldiers at that moment. The troops from Kvarc had also come down to Zalazje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And were those members of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, what were your orders for that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. There were orders that day that your komandir received. What orders did he receive that were passed on to you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes. He said we should get ready to go on, and we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We went from Zalazje through a wood and got down to Solocusa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you searching the terrain there, or were you still marching in a column?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: It was a column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told why you were going in that direction?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, nobody told me specifically why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you given any particular instructions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how long did you march? How long did it take you to get to the next location?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I think it was about 5 kilometres, so that means one, two, perhaps three hours. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to that location, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We came out at, or rather, we went down to the asphalt road running from Bratunac to Srebrenica at Solocusa, near the playing ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So now you are at or by Srebrenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes, nearby, although to the entrance to Srebrenica from the other side, opposite direction, is 1 kilometre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So now you're by the entrance as if you're going to Srebrenica from Potocari. That's where the playground is.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go into Srebrenica on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do? Where did you stay?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We were told to get away from the road and go into the houses, and that we should stay there and wait for further instructions, orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that what you did?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you in that area?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After spending the night there, did you receive any other orders the next day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what were those orders?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: A bus arrived. We got into the bus. We passed through Srebrenica. We arrived at Bojna, and we got out of the bus at Bojna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did -- I'm sorry. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: The battalion commander was there, Zekic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: And there was that transporter of ours from Pribicevac and the crew next to the transporter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us, if you know, who sent the bus over there.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got there, about what time of day are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: About noon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got to that location, did you get any further instructions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We stopped at Bojna briefly. The komandir talked to Zekic. I don't know what they talked about. But then we got back into the bus, and the bus drove us to the village of Ljubisavljevici which is next to Jadar, or rather not far away from Jadar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the purpose for going there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, we were supposed to search the terrain there, that's what I was told at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the terrain searched over there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: At Bojna, our komandir agreed with Zekic where we were to meet up after searching the terrain. And it was decided that this should be at the village of Kovacica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But my question was: Did you actually search the terrain? Because you said you were supposed to search the terrain. So the question is: Did you in fact search the terrain?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We passed by -- we took the route that we were supposed to take.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, how did you take this route, by foot? By bus?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: On foot. They are -- it's forest ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please describe to us the formation of the men when you were over there.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: They were all soldiers, soldiers from those villages who knew the area and who would be passing by their own houses. I was the only one to come from other parts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, what I'm trying to get at is: How were you searching the terrain? Describe to us the manner in which you and the other soldiers were physically conducting this search.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We took the road up until a certain place and then carried on. We would stop a little, take a look around, and carry on, that's what we did. But it wasn't a real search of the terrain. Our goal was to pass by there and reach the point we were supposed to reach.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were the soldiers spread out searching -- as they searched the terrain, as you marched forward on that terrain? That's what I'm trying to ask you.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We were in a group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How long did the searching of this terrain take?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Three to four hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said some of the soldiers -- or you were the only soldier that wasn't from that area. What did some of these other soldiers do, since they were from that area, if anything?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I remember a young guy who was one of the crew in the APC, he came to his house. We stopped there and then carried on. And he would say: "This is so-and-so's house, that's so-and-so's house." He would point out who the houses belonged to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that day when you were searching for three or four hours, did you find anyone? Did you come across any Muslim men or anyone?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any prisoners taken that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find any dead bodies in that location that might have been killed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find any weapons?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What did you do after that search? What was the next order?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We reached a certain collection point, as we called it, in the village of Kovacica, near Zekic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got to this collection point, about what time are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, it was afternoon. There were another two or three hours of daylight left before dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got to this collection point, what if anything did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Nothing. We had dinner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then what?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. From -- all right. And was your commander or the battalion commander, Zekic, there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: My komandir was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. From there, what did you do? You spent the night there. Where do you go next?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: The next day, we received orders to move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, move on to where?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We went down some routes and reached Srebrenica and the petrol station there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you went on these routes, to reach Srebrenica were you searching the terrain?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We took the road again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which road are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: The nearest road going through some villages down to the petrol pump.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. On that route, did you find anybody? Did you come across any prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you get to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We reached the petrol station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, which side are we talking about? Are we still back by the entrance by -- if you're coming from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes, the petrol station is at the entrance to Srebrenica from the Potocari side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you got to that location, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We waited for about an hour, and then the bus arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the bus arrived, where did it take you, assuming you got in the bus?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did it take you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: It took us to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got to Bratunac, about what time of day was this?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: It was sometime in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I'm sorry to interrupt, but somehow I lost the dates. Would you please try to establish that it's on the 13th and 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. What I was going to do now that we reached this point, I was going to show him a map that he looked and marked and go through the actual dates so that we actually have the actual locations with the date. And I was looking at the time and it would take about 10 minutes to do that, so perhaps we can have the break and then we can fill in the dates so we have a clear record. I first wanted to get the story out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And we'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to show you now what has been marked for identification purposes as D146. It has previously come into evidence, I believe the original map, as P369. Could you please look at this. And if we can put it on the ELMO. I have an extra copy for the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And just for the record D146 for identification is part of P369. And we've blown it up a little bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at this document, sir. Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you note on the document itself that there are some markings, some lines, and some numbers. Do you recognise those markings, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose markings are they?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: They are my markings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when were those markings made, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Last night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And in fact, on the larger map, the larger copy, you even placed your signature on it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you could please tell us - we're going to go step by step - number one, that location. What is over there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Here we have the starting out point, Pribicevac, to the first line is where we spent the night on the 11th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, just -- let's take it step by step. First of all, where you have the 1, that is where the forward command post was located of the Drina Corps at the time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes, Pribicevac was the forward command post of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we can even see that on the map. And 100 or so, 150 metres away is Kula where you had your trench, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe that where you said it was your impression that your commander had set up his forward command post during that period. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, yes, because he would be there frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, between 1 and 2 we see a line, you marked a line. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what does that line reflect?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: That line reflects the road, the route, that I took.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you said you left on the 11th pursuant to orders given by General Mladic to your komandir. How far did you get on the 11th? If you look at this map. About 800 metres from Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you designate to us or tell us where exactly on the map is that shown.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Where the line across is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So if you could reach over to the projector and you can point to us, maybe even put 11 there to designate --

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Pribicevac is here. That's where we spent the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Is it 1 or 11? Whatever you like. Do you want me to put 1 or 11?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Put 11 so we know it's the 11th of July. Can you put an 11 right where you spent the night.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, from there could you please tell us how far did you go the next day.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: The next day we started off from this point, took this road, and came to Banja Guber, went up Kozarica and reached this road here, the Srebrenica/Zalazje road, continued along that road and reached Zalazje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, what is the 2 for? Is that for day 2? What does 2 stand for?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes, it was the second day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where you marked 12 on the map, that's how far you went on that second day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes. And we spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the 13th, could you please tell us how far did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: On the 13th we set out from Zalazje here. We took this road -- actually, it was a path through the forest, and we came down to the road here not far from the playground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that's as far as you got on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And could you put there 13 so we know that that's the night of the 13th that you spent there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now on the morning of the 14th could you show us where -- what route you took. Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We got into the buses here and we went through Srebrenica. We passed Srebrenica and reached Bojna. And we had a rest there, a short rest, and that's where the transporter was, the APC. And then we continued along this road to Ljubisavljevici. And we got off the bus here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did you spend the night there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Where did you spend the night? How far did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We took this route, passed by Zivkovo Brdo, went across Siljato Brdo hill, and reached the village of Kovacica here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's where you would have spent the night of the 14th?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you put 14 there.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I've placed it there, yes, number 14.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so we know before we go any further, where is the area that you searched, you were asked to search? Could you just point that on the map for us.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We left the bus here, got off the bus. We took this route, Zeleni Jadar remained to our left. Zivkovo Brdo or hill on the right. We passed across Siljato Brdo or hill through some villages, called Saraci, Viogor and went down to the village of Kovacica. The broader region of Orahovac, but the village of Kovacica in particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you draw that in? Is it possible for you to sort of draw in with the pen the area, the general area, where you would have searched on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Where we got off the bus, we took this route. Well, I don't know if it's exactly like this, but anyway Jadar remained to our left, the ridge there by Zivkovo hill, Siljato hill, Viogor and the village of Kovacica. That was the first and last time I ever passed by that way. I was never there before and I was never there since.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But just so we have a record, so after you leave we know exactly what area, would you just with your pen mark that particular copy of the map the general area where you would have been searching.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I can't do that; that would be impossible. I couldn't even do it on a larger map, let alone this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. Okay. Could you tell us from the 14th, where did you go? You spent the night on the 14th; you've designated where it is. Could you tell us from there, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We went down this road passing the village of Bajramovici, we emerged on to this road here and reached the petrol station in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you spent the night there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you spend the night?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We waited for the buses there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And from there where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We waited for the buses and then got into the buses and then drove off to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what time -- when -- so this would have been what day when you got to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: It was always the -- it was already the 15th, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you told us earlier that at one point you went to the entrance point of Srebrenica and you spent the night over there in some houses. When was that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: That was at Solocusa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What day are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: The third day, that is to say, the 13th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So the 15th is when you returned to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what -- about what time would that have been?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, once you got to Bratunac, what was your next order?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We were given time off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How much time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: To spend the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then what? What was your next destination?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We spent the night, and then the next morning we got into the buses again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: And went along this road not far from the command of the 1st Infantry Battalion in the village of Magasici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And could you please point that out, if we could -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Bratunac is here, then this way to Magasici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that day would have been what day now? You got back to Bratunac on the 15th, what date would you have --

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, then it was the next day, the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Probably. And I think that coincides with the date when the 1st Infantry Battalion went to Zepa. It remained empty here, and we were given the assignment of being there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So are you sure it was the next day or could it have been later -- let me rephrase. How many days do you recall resting in Bratunac before going to --

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: One night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And when you got to this area, this location, what were your tasks? What orders were you given?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We were given the order to stay there until further instructions and orders. And that's what we did, we spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And could you please put a 16 over there so we know that this is the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now you said you spent the night there. Before spending the night there -- well, first of all, what time of day did you arrive there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We arrived sometime around, or rather, in the -- before noon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what did you do once you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Nothing much. We just spread out among the houses, and that's where we were. We were resting up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So I take it on the 16th you didn't do anything other than rest up?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you locate any prisoners that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any dead bodies over there on that day, in the area?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any abandoned weapons in that area?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The next day, the 17th, what do you do?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We spent the night there, one night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So that was the night of the 16th. So now we're talking about the 17th. What do you do on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: In the morning we were told to be ready and that we would be going most probably to some other location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall where you went the following day -- on that day? What was your next location?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I assumed the vehicle that was to have picked us up was to supposed to come from the direction of Kravica, but as the vehicle never turned up, we set out on foot and reached Bratunac walking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you walked back to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what time it was on the 17th that you walked back to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, it was about noon, perhaps a little after noon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. On your way to Bratunac -- well, first of all how long did it take you to get there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: It's quite a long way, 5 or 6 kilometres. It took us a couple of hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, from the place that you set off, okay, on the 17th, in which direction would Glogova be? Would it be on the way toward Bratunac or would it be in the opposite direction?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as you -- so then I take it as you were walking towards Bratunac you would have passed Glogova?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes. We passed through Glogova, because that's the way the road takes you, through Glogova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now when you -- could you please point out where Glogova is on the map.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You circled that area.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: That's the broader area around Glogova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you were going through Glogova, did you notice anything unusual going on over there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please describe to us what it is that you saw.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: When we were moving down from Magasici to the flat land down below, on the way I saw a freight train with a machine, a loader, digger, something big.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know where that machine was from?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How close did you go there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We passed by that truck, because it was along the whole road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you would have been near the truck, then, within -- a few metres away, then?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes, we passed by the truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you notice the -- any individuals over there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, there were a couple of people there around that trailer truck, as if there was something wrong with it and they were waiting for instructions. I didn't ask who.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask them what they were doing there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice if any digging was going on?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, this truck was standing on the road. It wasn't doing anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I'm not asking you whether this truck was doing anything; I'm asking you whether you were able to observe anyone digging anything, off the road?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice any graves, any patches of land that looked like they had been disturbed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I didn't notice anything at that time, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you notice it at another time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Later I did, later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "later," are we talking later in the day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, what time was it when you got into Bratunac on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We arrived sometime in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that period, after arriving in Bratunac, did you receive any other orders?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: We were given leave to rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How much rest were you given?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: A day or two. I think it was more likely to be just one day. In fact, only one night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And after that where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: After that we went to Zepa in the late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, I want to fast-forward to another period, 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, before you left this map I believe that the witness testified that he spent one night in Bratunac before going there, and we need a number there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And secondly, if you want to tender this document into the evidence, since the witness has already made some marks on this map, we need a new number on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please put on Bratunac -- I guess this would have been the night of the 17th when you returned to Bratunac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: It was probably the 17th, yes. It should be the 17th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can put a 17 by Bratunac; I know you already have a 15 there. Why don't you put -- why don't you mark 15 --

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. So that would be 17. Okay. All right. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do we have 15 there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Maybe I'm seeing things. We don't. I have it on mine because I put it there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you -- okay. I just want to make sure that I don't confuse you any more than I've confused myself. Before -- we have Magasici, we have 16. The night before going to Magasici, you were in Bratunac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The 15th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you could put a 15 as well?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And I apologise for confusing you. Now, we -- we said that the identification number was D146. We could put it -- we could designate it as D146 bis. All right. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We don't need the maps anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to move to another period; I believe it's sometime in 1996. Were you still with the Bratunac Brigade back then?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And could you please tell us what kind of position you held at that period.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
