utterances.text: After the Dayton Accords, they asked we show the VES -- from the VES -- from the civilian population. And because I had a place in the communications they offered me to take a course and to continue working in communications.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I accepted the offer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: And on the 20th of February I went for the training course and I returned on the 10th of March. The course was in Zalukovik. And there I was trained for -- and there I was trained to be a specialist in coding and teleprinter communications.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Before we go any further you said "VES." Just so we understand, what is that? What are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: V-E-S is what I have been trained to do in the army in which I served.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does it stand for? What is it exactly? Some of us didn't serve in the army, so we wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I think it's specialist military training. There's this abbreviation, VES, followed by a number, and there are different specialties such as infantry man, artillery man, rear man, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your training was in communications after Dayton?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I completed a training course and was trained to be a code person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, after your training, where were you working?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I came to the command of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you came back to the Bratunac Brigade, was Colonel Blagojevic still the commander, to your understanding?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us during this period of time whether you had any conversations with your commander, Colonel Blagojevic, with respect to any documents that you had located?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: When I arrived in the encrypting service in the brigade command, I found a situation that was not appropriate. I came across something that was not in accordance with the rules.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Such as?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: A person was working there who, in my view, was not a serious person. He left documents lying on the desk, in packages, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So what's wrong with that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: According to the rules, when I, as an encrypter, am given a document by my commander to encrypt and to pass on in code, I take the document, I process it, I write down the date and hour when I received it, when I processed it, when I forwarded it. And then in the records book, I write down when I gave it back to the person who had given it to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So that's the normal procedure?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what was wrong with these documents that you just told us?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: The documents should not have been there. They should have been given back to the person who had had them sent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, since you had encrypted -- since they were encrypted documents or documents that had been encrypted, would they have been of a sensitive nature, or does every document that's sent out encrypted?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Every document is encrypted -- well, not necessarily. But as a rule, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So what happened to the -- so when you saw these documents, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I concluded that this was not the proper place for them to be, so I called Colonel Blagojevic and said to him that the documents should be removed from there. He asked me why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your response?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I told him I didn't want them there because somebody one day might ask me for a document, a document might get lost, they would look for it, be unable to find it. And I said, well, this was not the proper place for the documents to be in the encryption room. There were other places where it was proper for the documents to be, but certainly not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what instructions, if any, did he give you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, what? Are you saying he didn't give you any instructions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: He didn't say anything. He said: Well, let them stay here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever ask you to destroy any documents?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, did you bring this matter up with anybody else, that is the documents, these documents, laying around?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I spoke to the security man, Momir Nikolic, and I put the same question to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was his response?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Nothing. He also said: Well, let them stay there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, did you bring it to anybody else's attention?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: When Momir Nikolic left to take up another business, he was replaced by Lazar Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: And I put the same question to Lazar Ostojic, and he replied in the same way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Eventually what happened to all of these documents, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Later on Savo Cvjetinovic became the commander, and he didn't take any steps to remove these documents. They were not just lying about in my office; they were lying about everywhere, in every office. Then Major Radic arrived, a commander who I view as a serious person. I said the same thing to him, that the documents should not be in my office, in the encryption room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what were the response that you got from this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: He issued an order that a team be set up and that these documents be archived by year, and this was done. And in my communications storeroom where the communications equipment was kept, a documents department was set up. Everything was put away in files, 1992, 1993, 1994, 1995. There were at least 50 or 60 files.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Who -- did you participate in this endeavour?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I didn't participate in it. Other people put these documents in binders and archived them and placed them on a shelf in that department.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I know that because I had the key to the storeroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us about what period, what time are we talking about, what year.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: All this happened in 1996. I don't know exactly what date it was when the documents were archived or when Major Radic became the commander. But as soon as he arrived, this work was done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know what happened to those documents?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: One day the investigators of The Hague Tribunal arrived and asked for access to the headquarters and the offices there, including that storeroom and those documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you still with the Bratunac Brigade or working in those headquarters when the folks from The Hague Tribunal came?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes, I was still there, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what happened when they came and they asked for access to the headquarters and the offices, including the storeroom of the -- and those documents?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: They went through all the offices. They looked in the desks. They took some maps. And finally they arrived at the storeroom where the documents were kept. They opened the binders and then they put them in their boxes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And so they took them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes. They packed them in their boxes. They said thank you, and they left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, from the time that they had been put in that storage room to the time that the folks, the investigators, from The Hague Tribunal came, to your knowledge do you know whether any of those documents were ordered to be destroyed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever asked to destroy any documents or hide any documents?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just finally, who had access to those documents?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: The personnel department, for example, the personnel officer. If he was looking for something from 1993 or 1994 or any year, he could come and take the binder, have a look inside, find the document, look at it, put it back, and so on. Anyone who was sent by the commander could have access.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when somebody would access these documents, was there anybody there to make sure the documents weren't taken away or weren't destroyed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: As far as I know, only rarely did someone come to make use of these documents. They just stood there and nobody took much account of them. They were practically just collecting dust. But I cannot exclude the possibility that someone came along and took a document out. I was not the only person who had the key to the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. While you were there, did anyone from the Main Staff or from the Drina Corps come along and ask to look at the documents or take any documents?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But as far as -- with respect to you, did anybody come to you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, I just want to go back and ask one last question, basically. I want to go back to the days from July 6th to July 11th, 1995, when you were up there in Kula and in Pribicevac. Based on what you were able to see, observe, your experience in being in the Bratunac Brigade for two and a half years plus, did you form an opinion as to what extent your commander, Commander Blagojevic, was engaged in what was happening in and around Srebrenica on those days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm objecting to that. There's no way that this gentleman can answer the question. It's entirely speculative. He's already testified that he didn't know Commander Blagojevic until somebody pointed him out to him at some point. So it's totally speculative. I don't see how he can answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. And especially you asked the opinion of this witness towards his commander at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking if he formed an impression, based on what he was able to see was happening. So he's a soldier, he's asked to put his life on the line, he's there for two and a half years. Here you have a commander who comes into his foxhole, basically, looking at maps all day long, nobody's coming to see him, nobody's giving him any orders. Surely this soldier would have formed an opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as the witness testified he had worked with Blagojevic later on, so the opinion at that time was somehow influenced by the later experience. I don't think there's any probative value in this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, thank you very, very much. I appreciate your candor and honesty in answering all of my questions. Mr. Lukic might have some questions; he represents Mr. Jokic. The Prosecutor undoubtedly will have some questions, and perhaps there might be some questions from the Judges. And I would appreciate it if you could be as honest and forthright as you have been with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic, do you have any questions for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Mr. Jokic's Defence does not have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do have a couple of questions. I'm just wondering if I can borrow the podium, please. Cross-examined by Ms. Issa:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've told us earlier that you went towards -- you left Pribicevac on the 11th of July and you stopped at some point 800 metres down from Pribicevac. Do you recall telling us that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how long were you there at that location before Commander Blagojevic got to your location?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but we didn't stay there long. Maybe after an hour or two, the colonel arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And how did you travel to that location from Pribicevac? Was it on foot or some other mode of transportation?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: This is terrain where you can only go on foot. It's very steep and the path is dangerous. We didn't know what there was down there. We were afraid of an ambush. We didn't know what was going on around us. I even thought we might be misused down there. I had all kinds of thoughts. It was very hard for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So you got there on foot. Now, you indicated that Colonel Blagojevic arrived approximately an hour or two after your arrival. So obviously he knew that -- where to find you, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Calls for speculation. "Obviously he knew." It's a bit speculative. We can draw conclusions that he found them, but that he obviously knew where they were, that's a bit speculative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think it's a quite natural consequence. You may proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer that question, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question. I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Obviously Colonel Blagojevic knew where to find you, since you've told us that he arrived at your location some time after you got there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: He did arrive, yes. I saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, turning to where you told us you spent some time between the 6th of July to the 11th of July in Pribicevac, from your position, sir, were you able --

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your position, were you able to observe or see into the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: From Pribicevac, you can just see a small section of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did you see any mortar rounds or artillery rounds hitting Srebrenica between that time period, 6 to 11 July?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No, there was no firing at Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You couldn't hear any detonations during that time period coming from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, according to the reports provided by the UN DutchBat at the time, during that time period, sir, there was - and I'll take an example from 6th July - they reported an: "Ongoing offensive launched within the enclave." And it said that: "The Bosnian Serb army used tanks, artillery, mortars, rockets, and they targeted the Bandera triangle, the DutchBat observation posts, and south of the observation posts, the Potocari township." You didn't hear any of that or see any of that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that from Pribicevac; it's impossible to see that. It's a broad concept.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just to correct myself, I said the DutchBat. It was actually the UN military observers, Your Honour, for the record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 10th of July, it was reported that the Srebrenica township was undergoing heavy shelling. They recorded figures of 49 shells since around 1.00 in the afternoon to 2.00. There was approximately nine rockets that was launched into the town and additional firing. You didn't see any of that either or hear any of those detonations?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I didn't hear any and it was impossible to hear that or see that from the position I was or notice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the air strikes going on on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that it was also reported by the UN military observers that the shelling of Srebrenica has been going on despite the air strikes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I ask the relevancy of this? Is this in dispute? This gentleman has not testified about whether there were strikes in Srebrenica or not. I just don't see the relevancy of this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that in the Prosecution's case, especially in the indictment, the indictment alleged that all those shellings created an atmosphere of terror, which is one of the ways to expel the Muslims from that area. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I thought --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it speaks to the issue of credibility, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the constant shelling of Srebrenica on the 11th of July, despite the air strikes?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I didn't know on the 11th of July. I didn't believe when Srebrenica -- it when Srebrenica fell. I don't know if any member of the Bratunac Brigade knew about that, at least the people I was with, that Srebrenica would fall and that it would be liberated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That wasn't my question, sir. I was asking if you were aware of the constant shelling that occurred on that day. Did you hear it or see it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I couldn't see anything from up there, and when planes turned up, I just noticed down there among those century-old trees where you couldn't see anything or hear anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So during that entire period between 6 and 11 July, it's -- what you're telling us you didn't hear or see any of the explosions coming from the direction of Srebrenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, no, I didn't hear them. It was -- there was some work going on to the left and right flank, but not Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you testified about a map that Colonel Blagojevic, you observed him during that period looking at. Could you tell whether that map was an artillery plan.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I don't know what map Colonel Blagojevic was looking at. There was a map, at least that's what I saw. There was a map, but what map it was I really don't know. I can't talk about that because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You've also told us that the -- you actually on the 11th of July advanced towards Srebrenica, and you indicated the direction that you went. So my -- right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question is: If the commander, the battalion commander, Zekic, said that his unit did not advance a single metre towards Srebrenica until the 13th of July, he would be wrong?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I don't know what Zekic said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm just asking you, sir, if he had said that, would he be wrong, in your view?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: In my opinion -- you mentioned the 13th of July. Is that it? On the 11th of July, we moved from Pribicevac toward Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if he said you hadn't moved until the 13th of July, that would be wrong. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: On the 11th of July, we moved towards Srebrenica, after Mladic's order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You also indicated, sir, in your testimony that at some point, I believe you had said it was the 15th, there were buses that arrived and you got on the buses as a means of transport. Can you tell us who arranged for those buses.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I don't know who organised them, but when we arrived at the petrol station, we waited for an hour or two. The buses turned up. They loaded us up, and then we went off to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know where they came from?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, no, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to Potocari on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that some of your colleagues from the same company that you worked out of were in Potocari, for example, Milomir Tanasijevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, he's not from the same company, number one; and number two, what is the relevance? And she can pose that question when the gentleman comes in the next day or so. What is the relevance?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, do you have any basis as for this person is from the same company?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: According to the roster, Your Honour. Perhaps I can pose another question first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't Milomir Tanasijevic part of the 2nd Company, 3rd Battalion, wasn't he at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: He was - how shall I put this? - disciplinarily subordinated to the 2nd Company, but the company commander was not in command of the transporter. So he could be treated as not belonging to that company, but he was there because that was the best place for that transporter, if it were ever to be used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But I didn't ask you if he was -- why he was there. I asked you if he was, in fact, part of the 2nd Company, and I understand you're saying he was.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was a member of the 2nd Company, judging by the lists. It's not my job to know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you were talking about the transporter just a minute ago, sir. Can you tell us what that is, what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: When from Magasici we set off for Bratunac, we saw the trailer truck in the village of Glogova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what does that have to do with Milomir Tanasijevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I don't know. Who said it had anything to do with him? The trailer truck with Milomir Tanasijevic, I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago, sir, when I asked you a question about Milomir Tanasijevic, whether or not he was part of the 2nd Company, you said he was there with the transporter, and I'm just trying to understand what you're talking about, what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't understand this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me just read your answer. You said: "He was a disciplinary subordinated to the 2nd Company, but the company commander was not in command of the transporter, so he could be treated as not belonging to that company, but he was there because that was the best place for that transporter, if it were ever to be used." What did you mean when you said: "He was there because that was the best place for the transporter"?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, somebody told him to be there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "there," what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, that place where that transporter was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that place?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: The transporter was at Kula for a time, then it was moved from Kula towards the command at Pribicevac halfway, and that's where it was. It was there while I was at Pribicevac. Well, we moved from Pribicevac on the 11th, I don't know where the transporter went, it, and what happened to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I don't know. I was down there in the forest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the transporter? What is a transporter?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: That transporter was intended in wartime to carry, to transport people, to pull out the wounded, that kind of thing. It was at Pribicevac as a sort of model, a piece of iron that didn't actually serve any purpose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can you describe it for us. You told us what it was intended for. Can you just tell us what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: The transporter had caterpillar tracks. It was 3 or 4 metres long, 2 metres wide, approximately. It had a turret. You could put a Browing [as interpreted], put a Browing [as interpreted] weapon, anti-aircraft machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you're talking about --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Browning, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you're talking about then, just so that it's clear to all of us, is an APC. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, yes, an armoured -- an APC with a small window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Just going then to when you passed through Glogova, sir, you said at that time you didn't notice the graves.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I didn't notice any graves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you also said later you did notice graves.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Several months later when I passed by through Glogova. I assumed what that was doing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So several months later you saw graves in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, once I did see that something was being done there that was unusual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you see?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I saw the ground -- bare ground, bare soil.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anything else?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see equipment several months later, digging equipment?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see any equipment, but afterwards I saw that people had been there and there was a yellow band denoting that place, and not only there, there was several places like that as you pass through Glogova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you were there in July, and I believe you said it was the 17th of July, didn't you smell anything unusual when you passed through Glogova?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No, I didn't notice any unusual smell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period, sir, did you pass through Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I passed through Kravica when we set out for Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you pass by the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: In the bus, along the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any bodies there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period, had you heard of anything occurring at the Kravica warehouse, any killings?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: That some incident had taken place, I did hear about that. We always had a small radio of some kind and we listened to the media, usually Sarajevo radio, and they would inform this happened, that happened. So I can't say that I didn't hear anything; I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, along the road to Zepa and at Zepa and after Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you heard it on the radio, along with your -- the other members of your unit, that there was an incident at Kravica warehouse. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, not only in Kravica, but the media would report that things happened in Konjevic Polje and elsewhere as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you're saying that things happened in Kravica and Konjevic Polje and elsewhere, are you referring to the killings that occurred there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, it said on the radio that there were killings and that before Srebrenica fell, too, that people were being killed. But the media will be the media. Even when nothing was going on in Srebrenica, things happened as broadcast over the radio. We kept hearing about things happening, even when they weren't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you heard specifically that the Muslims were being killed at the warehouse and in Konjevic Polje and elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: From the media, sort of, but specifically I didn't hear that from anyone. But the media did convey reports like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the reports they conveyed was that Muslims were killed by members of the army. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what they conveyed and reported, but generally that the civilians were killed. And we would listen from time to time, or rather, the road to Zepa was a very difficult road. We had to think about our own lives and protecting them. We weren't out on a picnic, you know, so we could listen to things like that. We first of all took those reports with a pinch of salt, the ones we heard over the radio, because we didn't know what was true and what wasn't true. And the media would report and say that fighting was going on around Zvornik, that the Tuzla Corps was attacking, that this was happening and that was happening, but I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, it's time for a break. Should we break now?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume at 12.00 -- 12.30, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, any re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very brief, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As always. Re-examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I just want to clarify a couple of points. You were asked about shelling, whether from your position you could hear any shelling. And I believe you said something to the effect that there were some -- you could hear activity, at least, from the left and from the right. Was I correct in -- is that what you stated?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, there were battles going on on the left and shooting on the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you hear that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Yes, you could hear that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to observe it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Well, as to the right-hand side, you could see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from your location, did that transporter, the APC, did it fire at all during those days?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: No, it did not fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that based on what you were able to see and hear and the activities that were going on, you did not believe that Srebrenica would fall. Would you please tell us why.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I personally didn't believe that Srebrenica would fall. I didn't believe that Srebrenica could fall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Because I knew from the intelligence reports that were coming in that Srebrenica was being defended by five brigades, that they had 15.000 soldiers under arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: And we -- those of us who were attacking, there weren't a lot of us. Not many soldiers had turned up at Pribicevac, just several units from Zvornik and so on. So there wasn't a lot of equipment there. And all the actions led by the Army of Republika Srpska prior to that had been unsuccessful. To quote an example, the attack at Gorazde wasn't liberated, Bihac was attacked and not liberated, Teocak, and so on. Other examples, Krusevo, up there. So that from my point of view, even the greatest optimists, those who wanted to liberate Srebrenica more than anything else couldn't believe that anything like that would ever happen, that Srebrenica could fall at all. And I believe that what could perhaps happen that we could draw closer to Srebrenica perhaps and to apply the principle which was applied in 1994, in May, around Gorazde. Because I asked about that Zvijezda 94, Star 94 operation a lot, because my house was there, so I was interested in learning more about it, in learning what had happened there, how many soldiers had taken part, how many -- how much weapons -- how many weapons were used, so that there was none of that at Srebrenica. There was an attack to the left and a little attack to the right, but Srebrenica is a very broad area. And the lines around Srebrenica, well I don't know. I'm sure that 10 to 15 kilometres around about. That's the circumference. It wasn't tied up, linked up. There weren't enough soldiers. We were dispersed too wide apart and we never knew whether we would be attacked from the front or the back or whether we would reach Pribicevac or whether we'd come across an ambush or a mine --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa. Witness, I'm sorry to interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: The answer is becoming nonresponsive at this point, Your Honour. It's just going on and on and on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Witness, the Defence counsel promised me that his re-direct will be very brief. I hope your answer to his question would be as concise as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll let you leave the courtroom as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me ask about another question with respect to your commander, Zekic. When General Mladic came and gave you and the company an order to head for Srebrenica, was your commander, Zekic, there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: Not at Pribicevac, no. At least I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether your commander told Mladic, after Mladic instructed him to go to Srebrenica, that he needed to get his commander's permission, Zekic's permission, to move on to Srebrenica as General Mladic was ordering?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's no foundation for that question, and I don't really see how it arises out of the cross-examination. And it's also quite leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We also believe that, Mr. Karnavas. That does not give you another opportunity for the direct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, the Prosecutor is trying to suggest that Mr. Zekic lied in court under oath when he said that his people did not move, his troops did not move an inch. It's clear that Mr. Zekic wasn't there. It's also clear from this gentleman that General Mladic ordered members of the Bratunac Brigade --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's totally inappropriate for Mr. Karnavas to put his argument at this point. The witness is still here and I think that's a misstatement of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may ask some questions along this line. Maybe they are not at the same location or maybe not at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that your komandir tried to locate Zekic to inform him that he had been instructed by Mladic to take the company towards Srebrenica on July 11th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you were asked about media and what you heard and whether you believed it and so on and so forth. Would it surprise you, sir, that since I began representing Mr. Blagojevic, the media has claimed I have been --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: This is totally inappropriate, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's not inappropriate and it goes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I have to know what Ms. Issa is objecting at.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: She hasn't heard the question. I'm entitled to pose the question. The cross-examination was suggesting that what the gentleman was receiving was accurate information from the radio at the time. Now, what I'm trying to suggest in my question is in my representing Mr. Blagojevic, the media from Sarajevo claims that I have been smuggling oil in Bosnia-Herzegovina, so if he knows whether that's accurate. I'm trying to make the point that the media in that part of the world is less than accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, first of all it started off as being a completely leading question. What Mr. Karnavas is suggesting is completely irrelevant to this proceeding, and we know that what the media was suggesting was accurate because there were, in fact, killings that occurred at Kravica. I don't believe that that fact is in dispute at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I don't think your question is totally relevant to this issue. I hope you could drop it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that you were hearing things from the radio, could you give us the exact date as to when you heard what was going on or what had happened in Kravica and from what media.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I can't know that. I don't know which media, what the radio stations were, what time. I can't really answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, could you tell us what month. The incident happened in Kravica warehouse on the 13th of July, 1995. Was it in July? Was it in August? Was it sometime later? Do you know? Can you help us out here?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: As to certain things, I don't even know to this day what I heard and if what I heard was true or how true, I really don't know that to this day, let alone to have learnt something afterwards. I heard that something had happened there, but I don't know what.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And finally, did you ever hear anything from the Serb media, from the RS, that proved to be less than accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAKULA
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't hear anything of any interest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. At this stage are there any documents to tender? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. D146, which is the map; and D146 bis, which is a copy or a section of the map which the gentleman marked in court during his direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections? Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. This document is admitted into the evidence. Are there any from the side of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. The usher will show you out of the room. We wish you a pleasant journey back home. You may leave now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, are there any protective measures for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: None, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you ready to call him this morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I wonder if I just may be excused from the courtroom, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us your name.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Milan Radic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may need to speak up a little bit and I'll ask you to speak a little slowly. Could you please tell us your last name letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Milan Radic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where are you from, Mr. Radic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: From Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you grow up?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: In Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the level of your education?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Secondary vocational school, the building construction stream.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you ever do your military service with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you -- did you participate in -- during the war activities in Bosnia and Herzegovina back in 1992 and onwards?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us when you were mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: The 5th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And where were you mobilised?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: The barracks was in Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to 1993, did you participate in the Territorial Defence that had been set up in Bratunac as early as 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So when you went to Han Pijesak in 1993, could you please tell us what sort of training you received, if any.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. I received infantry training, and that lasted a month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, what -- did you receive any further training?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: In Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of training was that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: It was communications.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long was that training?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: About six months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of that training? What sort of function would you be carrying out after this sort of six-month training on communications?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: This training was to use radio equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And after you received your training, where did you serve?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Close to Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you left Han Pijesak and moved to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was before my term of service expired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I don't remember precisely what the date was, but it was sometime in August 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So in 1994 sometime at or about August, when you moved to the Bratunac Brigade could you please tell us what position you held.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I was working in the Bratunac Brigade exchange, communications. And I had shifts near an elevation where we had equipment to maintain communications with the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I want to go step by step, and you may need to speak up just a little bit louder. You don't need to shout, but just a little bit louder. First of all, you said that you were working in the brigade. What exactly -- in the headquarters. What exactly were your functions when you were at the headquarters? Please describe them to us.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I worked on maintaining communications. I would work eight hours in the command at the switchboard, connecting lines at the command level for officers and so on. And then occasionally I was sent up to that elevation where we had that equipment, because I had been trained to use it. If there was no signal, if something broke down, I would be sent up there to maintain the equipment and service it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, before we get to the elevation, you said that you were connecting lines. Would you please tell us who you were connecting or what places were you connecting, the Bratunac Brigade headquarters with whom, these places.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Mainly the switchboard was in the building of the Bratunac Brigade, but it also had lines with the rear men and various officers and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What about with the corps of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. We did communicate with the corps, but rarely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you talked about this elevation. First of all, where is this elevation physically?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Physically, it's in the Bratunac area. As the crow flies, maybe 5 or 600 metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does this elevation have a name that you could identify it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's called Kik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. How do you spell that, letter by letter?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. It's K-i-k, Kik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Kik, all right. And at this elevation, at Kik, what is located?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: We had a shack there that we had built, and there was an RU-800 [as interpreted] piece of equipment there with a relay connection to the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what's an RU-800, just briefly, if you could describe that or tell us a little bit about it so we have a better understanding.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: It's RRU, there are two R's. It's a radio relay apparatus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what was the purpose for that RRU being there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: It was reached by a wire connection, and then from it messages were sent in code by teleprinter through a relay connection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were these messages sent to?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: They were sent to the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, was there other activity going on at that location, at Kik?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, could you please tell us what activities were going on and by whom.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: These were operators using a small piece of equipment, which was also an intercept centre. The operators were from the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So -- and I'm going to have to ask you to speak up a little bit louder. But if I understood you correctly, there were intercept operators from the corps working at Kik, at that elevation point. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they intercepting?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: They could intercept the course of events in the Bratunac area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, were they listening in on the Serbs or on the Muslims or the Croats?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, mostly the Muslims. The equipment had a range that was quite big, but for the most part it was the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you participate in any of these activities that were going on by these intercept operators from the corps?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Quite simply, I was there while I was servicing my equipment. If they were not there, if they had gone away for a few minutes, I would respond. That's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, you would help out?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, from what you were able to observe while you were up there at that elevation point called Kik, would you please describe to us what would happen to these intercepts, the information that was collected and gathered, what would happen to it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: They were sent by courier, packed in the normal way, as all the messages were in code. They were sent by courier to the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were physically sent as opposed to being transmitted in another fashion?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you say "no," were they physically taken there by courier or would you send them through the RRU-800?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: They were physically taken there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And where were they taken to, to which department? You said they were taken to the corps; that's Vlasenica, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, to the Vlasenica Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who would receive them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. There's been several leading, and we're getting to locations and all. It would be better if the witness could give us the locations and how they're gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the Drina Corps headquarters are?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we can go on. He's already given that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Since we're going to be making these sorts of petty objections, I would like to have an answer from the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the Drina Corps headquarters are?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: In Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know where the main headquarters are, the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I think it was in Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What about the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, do you know where they were, which city they might have been located?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The attitude directed in this manner is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm trying to speed it up, and it's kind of mind-boggling that somebody wouldn't know where the Drina Corps headquarters are when they're sending messages there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's very obvious where the Bratunac Brigade headquarters is located, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were these messages that were sent off to the Drina Corps, where were they analysed, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection on the foundation. There's no indication about any analysis yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If he knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If this is an important witness, we should do it right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those messages decoded, analysed, on spot, in situ, right there in Kik while you were there? Did you ever observe any of that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Only once, on one occasion we saw that. But it wasn't anything important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What would happen to these messages? Take us step by step. What's the process? Take your time.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: These messages were not sent. They went by courier. They were not sent by courier, but these lads told me what had happened there. If it was not something important, if they were not speaking in code but normally, they didn't even record those conversations or send them on. It was only if something was in code so we couldn't understand it, that it was taken down, packed, and then sent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when it was taken down, was it taken down in writing or was it actually recorded and a recording was sent? What was actually sent by courier?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry to object, but this is to foundation. So far we've heard that this witness was there -- was stationed in the brigade headquarters, that he occasionally went to this site, did not work on this, and perhaps occasionally helped out, but if he's going to ask these questions that we're all used to from the other intercepts, they need to establish how he knows any of this. We heard a little bit that some lads told him something, but if he was there for any length of time and how he learned, I think before he get into the substance, the foundation is needed so we know what he is basing this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the foundation is there. As you said, the witness testified that these lads told me what happened there, so I believe that the testimony of this witness is not the firsthand knowledge but hearsay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any messages, to your knowledge, sent to the Bratunac Brigade directly? Just to your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what period of time were you filling in, what are the months, in you can recall, that you would go to Kik?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: It wasn't strictly determined, but about once a month I would go and take a shift there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you do that all the way until July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on to another area, since this was not relevant, actually. Let's talk about July 1995. Where were you at the period when Srebrenica -- the events in Srebrenica occurred?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: As I used to go there, as I've said, I happened to be up there. I don't recall the exact date, whether it was the 5th or the 6th or the 4th maybe, I don't know. But my komandir gave me an order to get down from there and to go to the forward command post with the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Up there, we're talking about Kik?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during that period of time, just so we allay any suspense that might be in the air, did you hear any sensitive conversations? Did you participate in intercepting anything sensitive when you were up there in Kik, as you would go on occasion?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That was just part of your job?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you got this message -- first of all, you said it was from your komandir. Who was your komandir?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: It was a colonel, Dragan Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises, lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the message exactly, what were you to do?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: The message was that I should go to the command to be issued with my instructions, and in the brigade command -- from there I went to Pribicevac by car. I was given a piece of equipment with which to maintain communications with the brigade command. I went together with the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go step by step. First of all, had you been to Pribicevac before?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know what was at Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to Pribicevac at that point in time with your commander, did you know why you were going there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were given a piece of equipment, did you recognise that piece of equipment, and if so, what was it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, this was a piece of equipment I was trained to use. I was familiar with it. It was a field apparatus, radio relay apparatus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please describe it to us. Some of us may not have seen such a piece of equipment. So what does it look like?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: This set is called a RUP 12K, which means it has 12 channels. And the range is not significant. It's only used for communications at rather close range with the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give us an estimation of what the range would be.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I think perhaps some 10 kilometres or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Does that range -- is that range affected by the terrain in any way?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you linked up with anyone, this piece of equipment?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Only with the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that would be in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you linked up with any of the commanders of the battalions of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What about the Drina Corps, now that we know that it's in Vlasenica, were you linked up with Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, if he could help us. That's vague. What does linked up mean? It doesn't mean anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I haven't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It will be a long afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Linked up. Were you able to communicate between where you were and the corps in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you able to communicate with the other battalions of the Bratunac Brigade with that piece of equipment that you had?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were. But I did not receive from the komandir any papers with their frequencies. I only had the frequencies of my original brigade in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, why would you need their frequencies?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: How could I communicate with them if we were not on the same frequency? It would be impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, can I make this assumption that they had RUPs as well?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I am not aware of that. I don't know. They may have had one, but I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, could you communicate with this RUP 12K, if they had a Motorola, for instance?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what would they need to have, what kind of a piece of equipment would they need to have with them for you to communicate with them, assuming you had their frequencies?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Only if they had the same piece of equipment, the RUP 12.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know whether they had that equipment, the battalion commanders, had such equipment with them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I said that I didn't know about that, and I really don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you communicate -- well, let me back up. A foundational step. Did you see General Krstic while you were up there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where was he when you saw him.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: When we were put up up there in a house, let's call it the forward command post, he was some 30 metres away from us. There was some tents, and they had their devices and equipment, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you connected, linked up, able to communicate with General Krstic and his communications staff?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of communication equipment General Krstic had in his IKM?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever make contact with those individuals, I mean since you were a communications man, I would suspect that maybe some curiosity, did you ever go to speak with them and to see what they had?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. That's my specialty, and I was interested in finding out. And as they had people who were well-versed in that kind of thing, but as the commander did not allow me to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which commander are we speaking about?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you ever meet with these individuals and see -- well, first of all, who they were and what equipment they were using?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you got to Pribicevac, could you please describe to us what you did.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: We were put up there in a room. There were two beds, I think, or one; I don't remember. And a table. And that's where I placed my equipment, adjusted the frequencies, and checked the connection with my brigade in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in that building where that room was located with the two beds and the table and where you had set up your equipment, was that the same building that General Krstic and his crew were in?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else was in that building, if anyone?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, there might have been two other rooms. I know that in one there was that battalion or the logistics people from the battalion, and there was a bakery. They prepared food there. So I would see people, although I didn't know them. I was never there. Whether they cooked the food, baked the bread there, or whatever, but I would see them around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And once you got yourself set up -- well, first of all, where was Colonel Blagojevic when you were doing all of this?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic was there with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how close was he to you? Was he within sight and sound?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. Next to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And could you please -- before we go on to what you did and what Colonel Blagojevic did, who else was up in that area, that Pribicevac area? You told us there was Krstic, that there were some tents. We know that there is this building that you're in with a bakery and what have you. What else is located physically there, so we can have a pretty good picture?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, where we were there was what I said there was. And just beyond that, maybe some 100 metres away, on a small hill, hillock, called Kula, there were trenches there of that 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you ever visit Kula?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By yourself or was Colonel Blagojevic with you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. Colonel Blagojevic went with me. That was from time to time. We would go there occasionally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How many days were you up in that area? And let's -- let me just tell you that as a reference point we know that for a fact July 11th is the day that Srebrenica fell.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. So from that day, I don't remember the exact date, but on the 5th or 6th -- from the 5th or 6th to the 11th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please describe to us what you and Colonel Blagojevic did during those days, the 6th, the 7th, the 8th, the 9th, the 10th, the 11th. We'll go one by one. On the 6th, what were you able to observe on that particular day, as far as Colonel Blagojevic's movements, since he was within your sight and sound?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. Everything appeared normal. We spent our time there, in that room. There was a mist or fog. We would go outside and take a walk to Kula, go up and see the soldiers. I had some connections there. I took my equipment, and then we would go back to Kula. And we spent our time down there in that room. We would play cards or something or just slept. And on one occasion, I went to sleep on the bed. And Colonel Blagojevic went to sleep resting on the table. And he awoke and was astonished to see me, and I said: "Colonel, why didn't you wake me up from the bed?" He said: "No, no, just you go ahead. Keep on sleeping. No problem."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did he ask you to place any calls on that particular day, since you were the communications man?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No. Just the usual testing of the communication line with the Bratunac Brigade, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any calls for Colonel Blagojevic on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day did you notice whether Colonel Blagojevic had any meetings with any higher-echelon officers that might have been there on that location?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Concretely, did you see him and General Krstic conversing?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did General Krstic ever come over to that spot or to Kula where you and your commander were to meet and perhaps even speak with Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about on the 7th of July, was that any different than the 6th?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No contact with General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any contact with the battalion commanders, the 1st, the 2nd, the 3rd, the 4th?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any couriers come from the 1st, the 2nd, the 3rd, the 4th, or maybe even General Krstic to pass along any messages, if you are aware?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on then to the 8th. Surely something must have happened on the 8th, since nothing happened on the 6th or 7th. Did you notice anything on the 8th?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas is testifying, it also doesn't reflect the reality. This person said he didn't notice things, and Mr. Karnavas is now concluding that nothing happened. I think that's different and so the conclusions are inappropriate based on the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we understand that the witness answered no, means that he was not aware of anything happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just to make sure, sir, I only want you to see what you saw when Colonel Blagojevic was in your sight and sound for that entire period. Okay. Now, on the 8th did you notice if anyone -- did you notice whether Colonel Blagojevic had contact with General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
