utterances.text: Did you notice whether General Krstic was in that area on those days, on the 8th, for instance?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you -- do you remember whether on that day, the 8th, whether there were any messages that came through the communication equipment for your commander?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your commander ask you to get through any messages, to pass along any messages, since you were in control over this communication equipment?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- do you know where your commander spent that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Which day do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the 8th. You know, whether it was at that location or whether you moved to someplace else to pay any visits to any troops or ...

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No. I'm certain that at that day we were at Kula and went back down, had lunch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: And that's how the day passed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say you went back down, from Kula you went back down to where?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, 100 metres there, to the room we were stationed in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. When you went to Kula, what was your commander doing? Based on what you were able to observe now. I don't want you to guess. Don't tell me what somebody else told you, just what you were able to see when he was within your sight and sound.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: He had his map with him. I wasn't right up next to him; I was some 5 or 6 metres away. I was looking for a better signal for our equipment. But I was thereabouts, and what I noticed was that he was becoming acquainted on the map -- actually, he didn't know the names of the hills, so he asked people standing around about or people who were there: "What's this hill? What's its name? What elevation point?" Because this was an area he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And who was he asking?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, the people who were at that first trench, at Kula. Some soldiers, actually. I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, did you know these elevation points?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No. I was never there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then you said that you were trying -- you were a few metres -- 5 or 6 metres away and you were trying to get a better signal. Why were you trying to get a better signal? Were you trying to get a hold of somebody?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No. It was the only contact with the brigade, but it sort of got lost there. So I was looking for a better signal, should they happen to call.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me make sure that I have it right. When you would go to Kula, would you take your communications equipment with you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at any point in time, you're next to the commander with your equipment, in case he wants to use it or in case somebody puts in a call. Do I have it right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's like a backpack?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, in a sense, you could say that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the next day, on the 9th or the 10th, did you see whether Colonel Blagojevic had any contact with General Krstic or General Zivanovic or any higher-echelon officers?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On those days did he ask you to place any calls, perhaps to issue some orders to the men, to battalion commanders, to his company commanders?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, certainly not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the 11th, were you there in that area for the entire day, or did you leave at some point - we're talking the 11th, the day that Srebrenica fell - if you know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. We went from that room up to Kula about -- well, a number of times. We spent the day. We would come back sometime in the afternoon, 2.00 or 3.00. I don't know the exact time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, before we go on as to where you went after that, I just have one question with respect to Momir Nikolic, also known as Penzijica. That's his nickname I understand. Did you know Momir Nikolic at that point? Did you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know his position within the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether Momir Nikolic ever contacted his commander during that time when you were up there, the 6th, the 7th, the 8th, the 9th, the 10th, the 11th, you know, to perhaps pass along some intelligence information, since part of his job was head of intelligence?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him in Pribicevac and perhaps he wanted to have a tete-a-tete, a four-eyes and a four-ears conversation with his commander. Did you ever see Momir Nikolic in Pribicevac during those days?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the 11th, on the 11th of July, 1995, would you please tell us when you left that area with your commander, at what time, and of course I want to go step by step so we have an accurate accounting as to what happened on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is leading. He has told this person that he left with him on the 11th and now he's told him again. So I would prefer if we're getting into this that Mr. Karnavas not be the one who is telling this person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour, maybe I'm tired but I thought the gentleman indicated that they had left. But very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave Pribicevac on the 11th or did you stay there the entire time, the entire day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: We left Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time did you leave Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: As I said, I don't remember the exact time but it was sometime in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us: Where did you go to or where were you heading? Let's start with that. Where were you heading, in which direction?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, since we were already there at Kula and our trenches were down there somewhere in the forest, so we were thereabouts when General Mladic came by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when General Mladic came by, could you please describe to us what you saw, what you heard.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: We were there, and down there you could hear him coming towards Kula. He was shouting something out. And Colonel Blagojevic said to me that we should go to another trench so that -- so we went down a trench further into the forest. That's what we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: We went down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And first of all, did you know General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, by sight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when you moved and Colonel Blagojevic said to you that the two of you should go to another trench, in which direction were you heading, towards General Mladic or away from General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Away from General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a reason why, if it was expressed to you -- in other words, did Colonel Blagojevic tell you why you should move to another trench?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, not in so many words. The colonel, Colonel Blagojevic, didn't say anything to me, but I had the impression that he would like us to get a little further away from him because he was usually shouting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you get away? Did you go further down?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Not straight away. We were there for a time; however, they started towards us from that first trench, the soldiers who were up there started down towards us, and they said that they had been ordered to move and were moving toward Srebrenica. So they passed by us, and we asked them because we didn't know what was going on at all. So they passed by us and went through the forests. There were quite a number of them as far as I could see, but they were moving downwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they say who had ordered them to go and move towards Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: All they said was that they had received orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall whether -- do you know, first of all, whether those soldiers were from the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know them from before, but while we were there, yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And since you were -- where was your commander, Colonel Blagojevic, at the time when these soldiers went by and said: "We've been ordered to go to Srebrenica"?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, he was just by me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Close by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did he ask who had ordered them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see general -- any other generals at the time when you saw Mladic there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, as we stayed there at that time, Colonel Blagojevic told me to go and get some food for us from up there because we hadn't had anything to eat. And if we would go -- were to go down to the forest, in view of the situation, that we would have something to eat while we were down there. So I did go up to where we were. He stayed in the forest, Colonel Blagojevic, that is. Because I wanted to take a rucksack of food back down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me stop you here. Now, when you say you were down there and you went up there, where are you located at this point in time, physically speaking? We know where Kula is and you said there was some trenches. At this point in time, where are you physically located?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: From Kula, downwards, down the line, some 50 metres down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And that's where you first saw the soldiers coming in that direction?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, about what time of day is that? Do you remember perhaps from the light in the sky?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what time of day it was, about what time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't have a watch on me, but I assume it was sometime in the afternoon, perhaps 2.00 or 3.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you wanted to go back and get some food. Where would -- did you go back?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: The same way that I went to get there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But did you just go to Kula or did you have to go to the other place where you had the two beds and the table?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I went to that other place where we were in the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I see that our time is up. Perhaps we can pick up here tomorrow and continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, I'm afraid that you have to stay in The Hague for another day because we haven't finished your testimony. And during your stay here, you have to remember that you are still under oath, so do not let anybody talk to you and do not let anybody talk to you and do not talk to anybody about your testimony today. Well, we'll resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
